players.name: P. Beach
players.note: At 22 he's the kid keeper of the group, here off the back of helping Melbourne City lift the 2024/25 A-League title. First major tournament, so don't expect minutes, but he's the one quietly learning from Ryan.

players.name: P. Izzo
players.note: A late bloomer who waited years for his shot and finally debuted at 30, keeping a clean sheet against New Zealand. The patient understudy who took the long way round, via Melbourne Victory and now Denmark.

players.name: M. Ryan
players.note: The captain and the heartbeat, north of 100 caps and heading to a fourth World Cup, which ties the Australian record held by Cahill and Milligan. Saved a penalty on his 100th cap to help send the team to this tournament, so the big moments don't faze him.

players.name: A. Behich
players.note: At 35 he's one of the most capped Socceroos ever, a left-back who debuted back in 2012 and has barely missed a tournament since. The dependable old hand who came home to Melbourne and is still doing the unglamorous defensive shift.

players.name: J. Bos
players.note: An attacking left-back who earned a move to Feyenoord and promptly chipped in with goals and assists from defence. One of the genuine bright sparks of this squad, the kind of full-back who treats the touchline as a runway.

players.name: C. Burgess
players.note: A Scotland-born centre-back who plays his club football in the Championship with Swansea and helped see Australia through qualifying. Steady rather than flashy, the sort of defender you only notice when he's not there.

players.name: A. Circati
players.note: A 22-year-old centre-back holding down a Serie A starting spot at Parma, and after a month of pre-tournament camp he looks set to partner Souttar. Young, composed, and answering every question asked of him at exactly the right time.

players.name: J. Geria
players.note: A right-back and Melbourne Victory club legend who'd been out of the national setup for eight years before Popovic called him back in. Proof it's never quite over, even at 32 with 200-odd A-League games behind you.

players.name: L. Herrington
players.note: At 18 he's the youngest in the squad, a Brisbane Roar academy product who made his pro debut only in late 2024 and then materialised on a World Cup roster almost out of nowhere. A genuine bolt-from-the-blue selection who'll be soaking it all in.

players.name: H. Souttar
players.note: All 6ft 6in of him anchors the back line, and his older brother John plays the same position for Scotland, the country Harry left to play for Australia. A set-piece threat at both ends, which is what happens when you put the tallest man on the pitch in the box.

players.name: M. Degenek
players.note: Serbian-born and refreshingly blunt off the pitch, he's heading to his third World Cup with grit to spare. His club career has wandered from Germany to Japan to Serbia, and he brings that well-travelled steel to the back three.

players.name: J. Italiano
players.note: A Perth-raised defender who spent five years in Borussia Monchengladbach's reserves before finding regular first-team football in Austria. He once scored a hat-trick from defence with a couple of screamers, which is not the usual full-back job description.

players.name: K. Trewin
players.note: A ball-playing defender who swept Melbourne City's individual awards during their title season and only debuted for Australia in late 2025. The versatile type who can slot in almost anywhere across the back, which is exactly why he's here.

players.name: J. Irvine
players.note: Captain at St Pauli and one of Australia's most important midfielders, the engine who can both break things up and play. The Guardian's pick of the squad, though he's had to fight his way back from foot surgery to make it, which tells you how much this means to him.

players.name: C. Devlin
players.note: A defensive midfielder making a living in the Scottish Premiership with Hearts, the one who does the tackling so the more eye-catching names don't have to. Cut his teeth in New Zealand and Sydney before the move to Edinburgh.

players.name: A. O Neill
players.note: A defensive midfielder who swapped Belgium for New York City in early 2025 and gives the side a calm presence at the base. The kind of player whose value shows up in the spaces he closes rather than the highlight reel.

players.name: Paul Okon-Engstler
players.note: The son of former Socceroos captain Paul Okon, and now part of dad's old assistant-coach setup as a 20-year-old in his own right. Schooled at Club Brugge and Benfica's academies, he's the next-generation name to keep an eye on.

players.name: C. Metcalfe
players.note: Shares a Bundesliga dressing room with captain Irvine at St Pauli, a box-to-box midfielder who keeps things ticking. A Melbourne City product who's quietly built a solid career in Germany.

players.name: A. Hrustic
players.note: An attacking midfielder with a lovely left foot, now plying his trade in the Eredivisie with Heracles after spells at bigger German clubs. Wears the number 10 and carries the set-piece responsibility that tends to come with it.

players.name: C. Volpato
players.note: A Sydney-raised attacker who came up through Italy's youth ranks and switched his allegiance to Australia at the eleventh hour, landing in the squad days later. A Serie A creator with something to prove, and the most last-minute story in the group.

players.name: N. Irankunda
players.note: Born in a refugee camp after his family fled Burundi, raised in Adelaide, and once clocked as one of the fastest players to grace the Bundesliga. A genuine speed merchant now at Watford, and there's talk Popovic may even use him through the middle.

players.name: M. Leckie
players.note: The man who scored the goal that sent Australia past Denmark and into the last 16 in 2022, a moment that still gets replayed on loop back home. At 34 he's the experienced forward who knows exactly what these nights are worth.

players.name: A. Mabil
players.note: Born in Kenya's Kakuma refugee camp, raised in Adelaide, and later named Young Australian of the Year for his charity work with refugees. He scored one of the penalties that booked the 2022 World Cup spot, so the pressure moments are familiar territory.

players.name: T. Yengi
players.note: An uncapped striker until this squad, he forced his way in on the back of a loan spell in Japan that took Machida Zelvia to a continental final. The physical, out-of-nowhere bolter, and he spent years in his brother Kusini's shadow before this.

players.name: M. Touré
players.note: Born a refugee in Guinea, he became the youngest goalscorer in A-League history at 15 and now wears the number 9 in Denmark. Comes from a footballing family, with both brothers having played alongside him at Adelaide, and may well lead the line here.

players.name: N. Velupillay
players.note: A Melbourne Victory winger who scored on his international debut against China within minutes of coming off the bench, the dream way to introduce yourself. A quick, direct option off the flank who's earned his place through A-League form.
